chapters.title: Matter in Our Surroundings
chapters.unit: Unit I · Matter — Nature and Behaviour · 25 marks
chapters.brief: Matter as particles; particle motion, spacing and attraction; states and their changes, including evaporation and cooling.
chapters.briefHi: कणों के रूप में पदार्थ; कणों की गति, दूरी व आकर्षण; अवस्थाएँ, परिवर्तन और वाष्पीकरण।
keyConcepts: Matter has mass and occupies space; it is particulate
Particles have spaces between them, move continuously, and attract one another; heating generally increases particle kinetic energy
Diffusion: spontaneous mixing of particles; it is generally faster at higher temperature
Solids: closely packed particles vibrate about positions; liquids: particles remain close but move past one another; gases: particles are far apart and move freely
Melting / fusion and freezing; latent heat of fusion changes state at the melting point without a temperature rise during the change
Boiling throughout a liquid at its boiling point versus evaporation at the surface below boiling; latent heat of vaporisation
Evaporation rate is affected by exposed surface area, temperature, humidity and wind speed; evaporative cooling
Condensation and sublimation (solid directly to gas; deposition is the reverse); heating and pressure can change a substance’s state
NCERT chapter temperature conversion: K = °C + 273 (school-level rounded convention); pure water boils near 100 °C at 1 atm
learningOutcomes: Describe evidence for the particulate nature of matter and explain diffusion using particle motion
Compare the arrangement, motion and qualitative spacing of particles in solids, liquids and gases
Explain state changes by heating or cooling; distinguish evaporation from boiling
Relate evaporation rate and cooling qualitatively to surface area, temperature, humidity and wind speed
Use the school-level Celsius–Kelvin conversion stated in the NCERT chapter
reviewFlags: Track: CBSE Class IX Science (086), 2025–26. Unit I is 25 marks overall; this is not a chapter-wise mark allotment. This is a separate historical syllabus track and does not replace Class IX 2026–27 Chapter 1 (Cell).

NCERT 2024–25 Chapter 1 covers pressure and latent heat in more depth than the short CBSE 2025–26 outline. They are identified as source enrichment, not separately claimed as exam weightage. NCERT school-level conversion uses K = °C + 273; the precise ice melting point is 273.15 K.
The simulator is an idealised particle model at school level and supports, but cannot replace, NCERT activities and practical 6 (determining the melting point of ice and boiling point of water).
